title: Culturating i3LMNS Basic Protocol
author: Michael S. Fernandopulle
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5u5g6y6
materials: Prepare stock solutions of PLO, PEI, or PDL (see Table 3 ).
Gently tilt the plate to ensure full coverage.

steps.title: Apply coating solution
steps.instruction: Add one‑half of the culture volume of 1× coating solution (from step 1) to each tissue‑culture dish that will be used for plating Day 3 partially differentiated i³ LMNs.

steps.title: Incubate coated dishes
steps.instruction: Incubate the dishes for at least 01:00:00 at room temperature; for best results incubate overnight in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Dry and store coated dishes
steps.instruction: Aspirate all water from the dishes and let them dry completely in a biosafety cabinet (typically 00:30:00–01:00:00). To speed drying, stand dishes on their sides, lean them against the cabinet back, and leave lids slightly askew. After drying, use dishes immediately or wrap in aluminum foil and store at 4 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Optional laminin coating
steps.instruction: Dilute laminin to 15 µg ml⁻¹ in IM, add one‑half culture volume of this laminin solution to the polymer‑coated, washed, and dried wells, incubate at 37 °C for 01:00:00, then plate neurons by adding cells in an additional one‑half culture volume of IM.

steps.title: Prepare alternative coating medium
steps.instruction: If laminin coating is not performed, prepare warm IM supplemented with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor, 2 µg ml⁻¹ doxycycline, 1:10 000 Compound E (from stock), and 1 µg ml⁻¹ laminin. Optionally add 40 µM BrdU for 24:00:00 to suppress mitotically active cells, and optionally add CultureOne supplement from day 4 onward.

steps.title: Wash dishes with sterile water
steps.instruction: Wash each dish with sterile water, repeat twice for a total of three washes; if the coating is PEI, perform two additional washes (five washes total).

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension
steps.instruction: From frozen stock or freshly dissociated 3‑day differentiated cells, resuspend in the appropriate amount of medium. Typical cell numbers and volumes are: 96‑well plate (imaging) – 1–5 × 10⁴ cells in 100 µl medium/well; 8‑well chamber slide (imaging) – 0.3–1.5 × 10⁵ cells in 250 µl/well; 6‑well plate (biochemistry) – 1.5–2 × 10⁶ cells in 1.5 ml medium/well (supplement to 2–3 ml on day 5); 10‑cm dish (biochemistry) – 1–1.2 × 10⁷ cells in 8 ml medium (supplement to 10–12 ml on day 5); 15‑cm dish (biochemistry) – 3–3.5 × 10⁷ cells in 18 ml medium (supplement to 20–22 ml on day 5).

steps.title: Plate cells onto prepared wells
steps.instruction: Add the cell suspension to the prepared (coated and optionally laminin‑treated) wells using the volume specified for the plate format.

steps.title: Day 4 medium replacement
steps.instruction: On day 4, aspirate the existing medium and replace it with pre‑warmed MM supplemented with 1 µg ml⁻¹ laminin. Add the medium very slowly dropwise in the centre of the well while the plate is tilted until a small pool forms in a corner, then continue adding dropwise down the well wall onto the pool. If BrdU was used on day 3, wash the wells with PBS before adding the new medium.

steps.title: Monitor and change medium days 4‑7
steps.instruction: From day 4 to day 7, examine cultures daily under a phase‑contrast microscope for debris or morphological changes. Perform medium changes every 2–3 days by replacing one‑half of the medium with fresh MM + laminin. If high debris or clumping is observed, remove half the medium and replace it with a full volume of fresh medium (50 % increase). If debris persists after this extra medium, suspect insufficient coating or expired coating solution.

steps.title: Long‑term maintenance after day 7
steps.instruction: After day 7, perform half‑medium changes every 4–7 days with complete MM + laminin. For dense (biochemistry) cultures, change half‑medium biweekly; for moderate (microscopy) cultures, change weekly. Use a serological or micropipette to aspirate a measured volume slowly, tilting the dish so medium pools on one side, and dispense fresh medium gently toward the wall (away from cells). Avoid direct aspiration or dispensing onto the cells to prevent dissociation.
